newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund call sellers reign as futures gain.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund call sellers reign as futures gain.

text.p: Call sellers and volatility bears have dominated the Bund options market recently, although vol levels stabilised on Wednesday, dealers said.
Even as March Bund futures continued to nudge into new record territory, many in the options market were taking the view that further gains would be limited.
March Bund futures at 1442 GMT were at 102.86, off 0.05 from Tuesday, having earlier set a new record high of 103.18.
"The sellers were pretty much out in droves the last couple of days as far as volatility concerned in the Bunds," said Tom Chlada, senior trader at Nationsbank Europe in London.
"There were a lot of 103-104 call buyers back a month or six weeks ago. What they're doing now is they're selling and that's why vol is coming in," he said.
A trader at one London house said the break of 103.00 was not convincing enough to dissuade call sellers. "There's a lot of paper selling the 103.00 calls," he said.
But he added, "I think they're wrong. If we break 103.50 we might get an acceleration."
The trader added that at current volatility levels, call writers were not making big premiums for the options they were selling.

LIFFE end-of-day volatility levels on Tuesday showed March 103.00 volatility at 4.55 percent and June at 5.25 percent. The dealer at the London house gave higher volatility levels in Wednesday's session.
